questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of: pedestrian, zebra crossing, black spot, Highway Code.
questions.a: Pedestrian — a person walking along or crossing a road; zebra crossing — the striped place where pedestrians cross; black spot — a place where accidents happen very often; Highway Code — the book of rules for using roads.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What do the red, amber and green traffic lights mean?
questions.a: Red — stop; amber — get ready, stop if you can or prepare to move; green — go if the way is clear.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any six rules of using the road safely.
questions.a: Any six of: walk on a side path or facing oncoming traffic; look right, left and right again before crossing; cross at the zebra crossing; never cross in front of a parked vehicle; never play in the road; wear bright clothes at night; obey the traffic police and lights; wear a seat belt and a helmet; never board a moving vehicle.
accepted: left and right again before crossing
never cross in front of a parked vehicle
obey the traffic police and lights
wear a seat belt and a helmet

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any six causes of road accidents.
questions.a: Any six of: over-speeding; drunken driving; using a phone while driving; bad brakes and worn tyres; potholed roads; careless pedestrians; children playing in the road; overloading; driving without lights; stray animals; ignoring road signs.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Say what should be done at the scene of an accident.
questions.a: Keep calm and call for help (police or ambulance); do not crowd round the injured; give first aid if you know how; do not move a badly injured person carelessly; take the injured to hospital quickly; report to the police.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: You mustn't cross the road ____ it is clear.
questions.a: unless

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: The boy crossed the road ____ ____ ____ it was clear. (three words)
questions.a: as soon as

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Drivers ____ signal at junctions.
questions.a: must

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Join using because: Trudy was knocked down by a car. She crossed carelessly.
questions.a: Trudy was knocked down by a car because she crossed carelessly.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Join using so … that: The driver was very careless. He caused an accident.
questions.a: The driver was so careless that he caused an accident.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Join using when: He stopped. The light turned red.
questions.a: He stopped when the light turned red.
accepted: He stopped when the light turned red.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the adverbs formed from: careless, quick, heavy, good, angry.
questions.a: careless → carelessly; quick → quickly; heavy → heavily; good → well; angry → angrily.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write the pairs correctly: l____ and r____ (light/right); g____ and g____ (glass/grass).
questions.a: light and right; glass and grass.
accepted: light and right; glass and grass.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Use should always in a sentence about the Highway Code.
questions.a: Learner's sentence, for example: We should always obey the Highway Code when using the road.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) advising P.3 pupils on how to cross the road safely.
questions.a: Learner's paragraph. It should be one paragraph, in the present tense, with clear advice such as: stop at the edge, look right, look left and right again, listen, cross quickly but do not run, use the zebra crossing, and never cross in front of a parked vehicle.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a debate, and what is a motion?
questions.a: A debate is a formal discussion in which two sides argue for and against a motion before an audience. A motion is the statement being debated, beginning with "That …".

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any five people involved in a debate and the work of each.
questions.a: Any five: chairperson — controls the debate; secretary — writes the minutes and records the points; time keeper — keeps time and rings the bell; proposer — speaks for the motion; opposer — speaks against it; audience — listens and may vote.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the difference between a proposer and an opposer.
questions.a: A proposer speaks for the motion; an opposer speaks against it.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Explain a point of order, a point of information and a point of inquiry.
questions.a: Point of order — raised when a rule has been broken, for example insulting or going off the motion; point of information — giving a correct fact the speaker has got wrong; point of inquiry — asking for something to be made clear.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: How does a speaker correctly raise a point of order?
questions.a: The speaker stands up, addresses the chairperson, says "I rise on a point of order," states the point briefly, and sits down when the chairperson rules.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a suitable opening sentence for a speaker supporting a motion.
questions.a: Learner's answer, for example: "Mr Chairperson, honourable members of the house, I stand here to support the motion which says that…"

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a suitable closing sentence for a speaker opposing a motion.
questions.a: Learner's answer, for example: "With those few words, Mr Chairperson, I beg to oppose the motion. Thank you."

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any six rules of good debating.
questions.a: Any six of: address the chairperson; attack the point, not the person; keep to the motion; keep within the time; speak loudly and clearly; stand up straight; listen to others; accept the chairperson's ruling.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: ____ ____ the previous speaker said father buys clothes, mother loves me more. (two words)
questions.a: Even though

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: She argued out her points ____ people did not accept them.
questions.a: although

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: If I ____ (be) the chairperson, I would stop the noise.
questions.a: were

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Change to reported speech: "I support the motion," said Ann.
questions.a: Ann said that she supported the motion.
accepted: Ann said that she supported the motion.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Change to reported speech: "Sit down," the chairperson said to him.
questions.a: The chairperson told him to sit down.
accepted: The chairperson told him to sit down.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a motion of your own and give two points for it and two against it.
questions.a: Learner's answer. The motion must begin with "That …", with two clear points supporting it and two opposing it.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any four things a speaker should do before a debate.
questions.a: Any four of: read the motion carefully and know which side you are on; research the topic; write points in short phrases; put the strongest point first; think about what the other side will say and prepare answers; practise speaking.
accepted: read the motion carefully and know which side you are on
think about what the other side will say and prepare answers

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: the son of your uncle.
questions.a: My cousin.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: the daughter of your brother.
questions.a: My niece.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: the son of your sister.
questions.a: My nephew.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: your brother's wife.
questions.a: My sister-in-law.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: the mother of your husband or wife.
questions.a: My mother-in-law.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the difference between a half-brother and a stepbrother.
questions.a: A half-brother shares one parent with you; a stepbrother is the son of your stepparent and shares no parent with you.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: three children born at the same birth.
questions.a: Triplets.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is your mother to your father's mother?
questions.a: She is her daughter-in-law.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Draw a simple family tree showing your grandparents, your parents, yourself and one cousin.
questions.a: Learner's family tree. It should use an equals sign for marriage, vertical lines from parents to children, and place each generation on its own level.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in: My aunt is married ____ a headteacher.
questions.a: to

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in: He shared the money ____ his three brothers. (between / among)
questions.a: among

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in: My uncle has ____ arrived; he came a minute ago.
questions.a: just

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in: The visitors have ____ eaten, so do not cook for them.
questions.a: already

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Fill in the correct word: Sarah is ____ than her cousin. (elder / older)
questions.a: older

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Use eldest in a sentence of your own.
questions.a: Learner's sentence, for example: My eldest brother is a teacher.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of: densely populated and sparsely populated.
questions.a: Densely populated means having many people in a small area; sparsely populated means having few people in a large area.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one reason why a town is usually densely populated.
questions.a: Because towns have jobs, schools, hospitals, electricity, water and business opportunities, which attract many people.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write four sentences describing the relationships in your family.
questions.a: Learner's answer. Each sentence should show one relationship clearly, for example: My mother's sister is my aunt.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What should a child do if an adult threatens or abuses him or her?
questions.a: The child should say NO, get away and tell a trusted adult at once — a parent, teacher, religious leader, health worker or the police. It must never be kept secret, and it is never the child's fault.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) about your family.
questions.a: Learner's paragraph. It should be one paragraph, name the family members and their relationships, use correct family words and correct punctuation.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any six tools used by a carpenter and say what each is used for.
questions.a: Any six: saw — cutting wood; plane — smoothing wood; hammer — driving in nails; drill — making holes; screwdriver — driving in screws; sandpaper — smoothing a surface; tape measure — measuring.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Describe, using first, next, then and finally, how a carpenter makes a stool.
questions.a: Learner's answer, for example: First he measures and marks the wood, next he cuts it with a saw, then he planes it smooth and joins the pieces with nails, and finally he sands it and applies varnish.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Change to the passive: The carpenter is making a table.
questions.a: A table is being made by the carpenter.
accepted: A table is being made by the carpenter.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Change to the passive: The tailor has finished my shirt.
questions.a: My shirt has been finished by the tailor.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any six items used by a tailor and say what each is used for.
questions.a: Any six: sewing machine — stitching; needle — hand sewing; thread — sewing; tape measure — taking measurements; scissors — cutting cloth; thimble — protecting the finger; bobbin — holding the lower thread.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: the line where two pieces of cloth are joined.
questions.a: A seam.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: the small object worn on a finger to protect it when sewing.
questions.a: A thimble.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Be careful ____ stitching the cloth, because you may hurt your finger.
questions.a: when

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Robert prefers sewing ____ knitting.
questions.a: to

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any six things used in baking and say what each is used for.
questions.a: Any six: oven — baking; baking tin — holding the dough; sieve — sifting flour; rolling pin — rolling out dough; cookie cutter — cutting shapes; yeast — making dough rise; icing sugar — decorating.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is the work of yeast in baking? What does knead mean?
questions.a: Yeast makes the dough rise so that the bread or cake is soft and light. To knead is to press and fold the dough with the hands until it is smooth.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write out five steps of baking cakes, in order.
questions.a: Learner's answer, for example: sieve the flour → mix the margarine and sugar → add eggs and flour and knead → put the dough in a greased tin → bake in a hot oven, then cool and decorate.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Don't forget ____ ____ the oven. (two words)
questions.a: to shut

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the difference between used to and is used for, with an example of each.
questions.a: Used to shows a habit in the past: I used to bake cakes when I was young. Is used for shows purpose: A spoon is used for mixing butter and sugar.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Form nouns from: bake, mix, decorate, measure, teach.
questions.a: bake → baker/bakery/baking; mix → mixture; decorate → decoration; measure → measurement; teach → teacher/teaching.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any six ways of caring for animals.
questions.a: Any six of: give clean water and enough feed; build a clean dry shelter; treat and vaccinate them; dip or spray against ticks; handle them gently; give them space; protect them from thieves and bad weather; never beat or overwork them; call a veterinary officer when they are sick.
accepted: give clean water and enough feed
protect them from thieves and bad weather
call a veterinary officer when they are sick

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of: welfare, docking, tethering, stray.
questions.a: Welfare — the good condition and comfort of an animal; docking — cutting short an animal's tail; tethering — tying an animal with a rope to a peg; stray — an animal wandering with no owner.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Not only ____ ____ feed animals but also treat them when they are sick.
questions.a: should you

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give three ways in which animals show how they feel.
questions.a: Any three, for example: a dog wags its tail when happy and growls when angry; a cow lows when hungry or looking for its calf; a hen clucks to call its chicks; a sick animal becomes dull and quiet and refuses to eat.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short paragraph (about six sentences) about an occupation you would like to do when you grow up.
questions.a: Learner's paragraph. It should name the occupation, give reasons for the choice, mention some of its tools or activities, and be written in one paragraph with correct punctuation.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any five workers in a hotel and give the duty of each.
questions.a: Any five: waiter/waitress — serves food and drinks at table; chef — cooks the food; receptionist — receives guests and books rooms; manager — is in charge of the hotel; porter — carries guests' luggage.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the meaning of: menu, bill, receipt, cutlery, serviette.
questions.a: Menu — the list of food and drinks with prices; bill — the paper showing how much a customer must pay; receipt — the paper showing that payment has been made; cutlery — knives, forks and spoons; serviette — the cloth or paper used to wipe the mouth and hands.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the difference between checking in and checking out.
questions.a: Checking in is arriving at a hotel and registering for a room; checking out is leaving the hotel and paying the bill.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name any six places found in a big hotel.
questions.a: Any six of: reception, restaurant, dining room, lounge, bar, conference room, washrooms, gym, sauna, swimming pool, kitchen, balcony.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Name the four meals mentioned in the syllabus and say when each is taken.
questions.a: Breakfast — in the morning; lunch — in the middle of the day; supper — in the evening; dinner — the main meal, usually in the evening.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a dessert? Give three examples.
questions.a: A dessert is the sweet dish taken at the end of a meal. Examples: fruit, jelly, pudding (also ice cream, cake).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short lunch menu for a hotel, with at least five items and their prices.
questions.a: Learner's menu. It should have the hotel name and meal at the top, at least five items grouped sensibly, and a price against each.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: ____ I have the bill, please?
questions.a: May

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: No sooner had the guest finished eating ____ he asked for the bill.
questions.a: than

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: The school ____ hold its party in the hotel conference room.
questions.a: may

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the adjectives formed from: comfort, enjoy, beauty, expense, taste.
questions.a: comfort → comfortable; enjoy → enjoyable; beauty → beautiful; expense → expensive; taste → tasty.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Punctuate correctly: may i have the menu please said the guest
questions.a: "May I have the menu, please?" said the guest.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a four-line dialogue between a waiter and a customer ordering a meal.
questions.a: Learner's dialogue. It must name each speaker, start a new line for each, use quotation marks or the play format consistently, and use polite language such as May I …, please.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any six good table manners.
questions.a: Any six of: wash hands before eating; sit upright; place the serviette on your lap; use the cutlery properly; do not talk with your mouth full; chew with your mouth closed; do not make noise with the cutlery; say please and thank you; ask to be excused before leaving the table.
accepted: place the serviette on your lap
do not talk with your mouth full
do not make noise with the cutlery
ask to be excused before leaving the table

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short advertisement (about four lines) for a hotel in your town.
questions.a: Learner's advertisement. It should have the hotel name, a catchy line, the services, the price or an offer, the location and a contact.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a dictionary? Give any four things it tells you about a word.
questions.a: A dictionary is a book that lists words in alphabetical order and gives information about them. Any four of: spelling, meaning, pronunciation, stress, part of speech, plural form, origin, example sentence.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What is a thesaurus, and how is it different from a dictionary?
questions.a: A thesaurus is a book that gives words of similar meaning (synonyms) and opposites. A dictionary explains what a word means, while a thesaurus offers other words you could use instead.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Arrange in alphabetical order: orange, apple, mango, banana, pear.
questions.a: apple, banana, mango, orange, pear

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Arrange in alphabetical order: stand, stamp, state, star, stay.
questions.a: stamp, stand, star, state, stay

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Arrange in alphabetical order: chief, chair, child, chalk, cheese.
questions.a: chair, chalk, cheese, chief, child

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What are guide words?
questions.a: Guide words are the two words at the top of a dictionary page: the first word on that page and the last word on that page.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: If the guide words on a page are father — feather, which of these words are on that page: fast, feast, feed, fault?
questions.a: feast is on that page. Fast comes before father, and feed and fault fall outside the range.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: What do these abbreviations stand for: n., v., adj., adv., pl.?
questions.a: n. — noun; v. — verb; adj. — adjective; adv. — adverb; pl. — plural.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write out what this entry tells you: quick /kwɪk/ adj. fast; taking a short time.
questions.a: It tells you the spelling (quick), the pronunciation /kwɪk/, that it is an adjective, and its meaning — fast, taking a short time.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give one word for: a word formed from the first letters of other words, and give two examples.
questions.a: An acronym. Examples: UNEB, NEMA (also UWA, NGO, AIDS).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Add question tags: A dictionary gives meanings, ____? · She isn't reading, ____? · I am late, ____?
questions.a: doesn't it? · is she? · aren't I?

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the opposites of: cheap, arrive, polite, shallow, ancient.
questions.a: cheap → expensive; arrive → depart; polite → rude; shallow → deep; ancient → modern.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the opposites by adding a prefix: happy, possible, legal, agree, behave.
questions.a: happy → unhappy; possible → impossible; legal → illegal; agree → disagree; behave → misbehave.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give the comparative and superlative of: tall, big, happy, expensive, good, bad.
questions.a: tall — taller — tallest; big — bigger — biggest; happy — happier — happiest; expensive — more expensive — most expensive; good — better — best; bad — worse — worst.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Complete: Peach comes ____ people in the dictionary, and people comes ____ peach.
questions.a: Peach comes before people, and people comes after peach.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Give any five reasons why a dictionary is important to a P.6 learner.
questions.a: Any five of: it gives correct spellings; it explains new words; it shows pronunciation; it gives the part of speech; it improves vocabulary and composition; it settles arguments about meaning; it helps in reading and research.
accepted: it gives the part of speech
it helps in reading and research

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Which word would come first in a dictionary: market or marble? Give a reason.
questions.a: Marble, because after mar- we compare the fourth letter: b comes before k.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Use most useful correctly in a sentence.
questions.a: Learner's sentence, for example: A dictionary is the most useful book in the classroom.

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Find and write any three words in this note that would appear on a dictionary page with the guide words sound — spelling.
questions.a: Any three words falling between sound and spelling alphabetically, for example sounds, speech, spell (also speaker, special).

questions.subject: ENG
questions.q: Write a short paragraph (about five sentences) explaining to a P.4 pupil how to look up a word in a dictionary.
questions.a: Learner's paragraph. It should tell the pupil to know the first letter of the word, open the dictionary near that letter, use the guide words at the top of the page, follow the letters one by one, and then read the meaning and the part of speech.
